entry.title: Can agents run research and robots?

media:group.media:title: Can agents run research and robots?
media:group.media:description:
Can AI agents do more than answer questions? In this October 7th episode of GenerAIly Speaking, hosts Jay Busch and Bharathi Srinivasan put that to the test with two demos. First, Madhu Samhitha Vangara and Tejas Kashinath build a research agent from scratch with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It searches the web, arXiv, Hacker News, and GitHub, remembers who you are, and reports back as a noir detective, a sports announcer, or a Greek bard. Afterward, we talk about where research agents could go next, from agents that read research to agents that run experiments on their own, like Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch project. Next, Kiowa Jackson and Cole Harrison show how a humanoid robot policy is trained and evaluated on AWS. Using the AWS Physical AI Toolchain, they follow NVIDIA GR00T from fine-tuning in Amazon SageMaker to testing in NVIDIA Isaac Lab Arena, with a success gate it has to pass before it's registered. Along the way, we discuss robot-use agents, the idea from MIT professor Phillip Isola's recent essay that a general AI agent could use a robot as a tool.
Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/getting-started/
Try the AgentCore getting started workshop https://catalog.workshops.aws/agentcore-getting-started/en-US
Explore the Arena workflow in the AWS Physical AI Toolchain https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-aws-physical-ai-toolchain/tree/development/isaac-lab-arena-on-aws

entry.title: Lost Glacier: Scaling regenerative agriculture with AWS AI | Amazon Web Services

media:group.media:title: Lost Glacier: Scaling regenerative agriculture with AWS AI | Amazon Web Services
media:group.media:description:
Lost Glacier is working to fix agriculture by giving farmers the digital tools they need to leave the land better than when they started. The organization focuses on regenerative agriculture, helping farmers capture and verify the sustainable practices they use every day.
Using AWS, Lost Glacier built a platform that fits seamlessly into farmers' lives. Farmers can snap a photo, leave a voice note, or log their activities from a smartphone. That data is geolocated, uploaded online or offline, and processed to verify carbon farming practices. The platform uses AI to predict changes in soil organic carbon over time, a key indicator of soil health and productivity.
Through the AWS Social Entrepreneur Accelerator, Lost Glacier gained access to cloud resources, tools, and expert guidance that transformed what was possible for their team. The program helped them understand and apply AWS technology to build a scalable solution now being tested across living labs in the EU.
